- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-forecast using sentiment-weighted average of recent 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms in early periods (days 1–7) when sentiment is volatile; apply 1–2% upward bias for first 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3-period moving average of true values.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral or bearish), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for hidden risk aversion.
